license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.

title: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian — Central American Federation
license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.
note: Formation in 1823 and dissolution process during 1838–1840. Only source phases through 1837 are retained; no complete federation is shown after secessions begin.

title: Congreso de la República del Perú — Archivo Digital de la Legislación del Perú
license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.
note: Confederation established 28 October 1836; separate 1839 Peruvian constitution. The transition year 1839 is omitted because the annual source cannot show the collapse precisely.

title: Museo Histórico Sarmiento — Disolución de la Confederación Argentina
license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.
note: Confederation dissolved in December 1861. Generic Argentina labels avoid carrying the source's Confederation name through 1885.

title: Banco de la República — Constituciones de Colombia
license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.
note: Constitutional titles distinguish Estados Unidos de Colombia (1863) from República de Colombia (1886). The dataset's generic Republic of Colombia label for 1866–1885 is corrected without changing its polygon.

title: Arquivo Nacional, Brasil — Período Imperial (1822 a 1889)
license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.
note: Brazil's independence was proclaimed in 1822. The source Portuguese 1820–1823 phase is restricted to 1820–1821 to avoid extending the undifferentiated colonial polygon over the new empire.

title: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian — Dominican Republic
license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.
note: Dominican independence in 1844 and Spanish rule 1861–1865. Omit source Haiti coverage in 1844–1845 and withhold Dominican colonial components rather than extend an undifferentiated Spanish source phase.

title: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division — Country Profile: Haiti
license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.
note: The republic was suspended during the 1849–1859 empire. Generic Haiti labels avoid the source's Empire of Haiti label across incompatible regimes.

title: Nationaal Archief — Koloniale geschiedenis
license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.
note: Historical West Indies coverage includes Suriname and the Antilles. Generic Dutch American possessions avoids applying the source's Netherlands Antilles label to mainland Suriname.

title: Ministerio de Cultura, España — The Last Territories
license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.
note: Cuba and Puerto Rico remained Spanish after continental independence. From 1824 onward retain only their whole source components; reject stale Lima, La Paz, Chiloé, Río Negro and Falkland components. Dominican annexation is not reconstructed here.

license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.
note: Abdication in March 1823; omit the source's 1823 imperial year rather than show the empire in the December 31 snapshot.

license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.

title: INEHRM — Centralismo
license: Source linked for chronology/label checking; no source text or geometry reproduced.
